notes_for_us: Nothing in the catalogue expresses a landing zone, and this prompt is about landing. hazard-kill is the opposite of what is wanted, checkpoint-respawn is a pad you touch on the way up, and winner-zone is the roof. A soft-landing target — water, hay, airbag, deep snow — is a real and common Roblox request with no ID.

Tower Obby was the only preset whose shape matched, and it brought obstacle-timing with it. The brief's instruction to keep uncontradicted preset options is easy to follow here, but the honest reading is that a first-time user asking to 'climb a building and have fun' would be surprised by disappearing platforms.

notes_for_us: Almost the entire prompt is scripting specification — raycast lengths, stud dimensions, velocity values — and only its last four bullets are the map. Step 0 handled that cleanly, but note that the numbers inside the mechanics text are the ones that constrain the layout: '12x12x2 stud asphalt part', 'raycast 3 studs left/right', '100-stud raycast'. Those are spatial tolerances the map has to satisfy and they survive only as prose in mechanics, where no layout consumer will look for them.

No option expresses a grind rail, and it is the defining traversal feature of a whole class of Roblox movement games. Nothing in the catalogue is close: cover breaks sightlines, path-* rows are ground routes, and teleporter-link moves you instantly.

notes_for_us: Three quarters of this prompt is theme and the handoff handles that well — theme is free text, so 'Strawberry Shortcake land' survives intact rather than being flattened into Stylized / Toon. The prompt says 'tycoon' and nothing else about the loop, so all three of the build's picks are the preset's. That is the padding pattern the brief warns about, but here it is hard to call it wrong: Tycoon's three options are what the word tycoon means. The measurement to watch is whether preset_derived counts distinguish 'the preset invented this' from 'the genre word implied this'.
